title: Work IQ: how agents reach Microsoft 365 and business data, and what an admin can switch off
summary: The documented controls, commands and billing claims pass the independent check. Two minor qualifications remain: Microsoft distinguishes generally available Business Applications access from preview experiences, and the general environment Features reference also requires System Administrator security permissions.

claims.claim: Work IQ is Microsoft's workplace intelligence layer for agents and applications.
claims.quote: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data, context, and tools.

claims.claim: Work IQ lets agents reason over Microsoft 365 data with permission-aware governance.
claims.quote: It continuously builds a semantic understanding across Microsoft 365 and external systems with built-in, permission-aware governance.

claims.claim: Work IQ includes business data from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform.
claims.quote: In addition to productivity data from Microsoft 365 applications, Work IQ also includes business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is described as preview.
claims.quote: Some workloads, such as Business apps (preview), are available in preview and require you to turn on preview workloads in the agent's settings.
claims.fix: Qualify the blanket preview wording: 'The Copilot Studio page labels Business apps as preview; the Power Apps user guide says access through Work IQ MCP and Copilot Studio is generally available, while Cowork access is public preview.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/user/use-business-apps-work-iq to sources; it states: 'Access to Business Applications through Work IQ Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Microsoft Copilot Studio is generally available. Access through Cowork is available in public preview.'

claims.quote: Work IQ supports A2A for agent-to-agent collaboration and REST for web application interactions

claims.quote: The Work IQ MCP server exposes Microsoft 365 intelligence capabilities and connected enterprise sources to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

claims.claim: Work IQ can be reached through a REST API.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.quote: Work IQ supports A2A for agent-to-agent collaboration and REST for web application interactions, enabling agents to delegate work, maintain continuity, and deliver fully processed, Copilot-quality responses.

claims.claim: Context assembles grounded inputs without requiring agents to manage retrieval pipelines.
claims.quote: Work IQ assembles and grounds context internally across organizational and business data to provide agent-ready inputs, so agents don't need to stitch together raw signals or manage retrieval pipelines.

claims.claim: Generic MCP tool verbs such as fetch, create and update act on resource paths.
claims.quote: These tools function as simple verbs (such as fetch, create, and update), while resource paths define what the agent is working with.

claims.claim: Workspaces use SharePoint Embedded working storage for intermediate data and outputs.
claims.quote: SharePoint Embedded working storage gives agents a persistent space within your Microsoft 365 tenant boundary to manage intermediate data and outputs
